maria: hey @sam — first day! I can authenticate to the cluster but when I try `kubectl get pods -n maria-dev` I get `Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User \"u:maria\" cannot list resource \"pods\" in API group \"\" in the namespace \"maria-dev\"`. I also don't see `maria-dev` in `kubectl get ns`.

sam: welcome! :wave: quick checklist — which context are you on? run `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl config get-contexts` first. Also try `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n maria-dev`.

maria: current-context is `redwood-dev@oidc`. here's the output I pasted: 
```
kubectl auth can-i get pods -n maria-dev
no
```

sam: ok that means your SSO identity hasn't been granted access to that namespace yet. For new hires we normally provision a per-user namespace after they complete the onboarding access form: https://redwood.internal/onboard/ns-request — include your GitHub handle and team (frontend/backend). I can start the request for you if you want.

linda: hey @maria — eng-infra here. We do have an automated step but it requires the SSO Kube Access app approval and the AUP signed. Go to https://id.redwood.com -> Applications -> Kube Access -> Approve. After you approve, run `rctl sync` (our CLI syncs your SSO groups into RBAC). Once that's done ping me and I'll confirm namespace create/rolebinding.

devex-bot: friendly reminder — your initial kubeconfig issued by the onboarding flow will expire in 14 days. Rotate with `rctl rotate-kubeconfig` or follow the console flow at https://console.redwood.internal/account/keys.

maria: I approved the app and signed the AUP. ran `rctl sync` and then `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n maria-dev` now returns `yes`. I can see the namespace! :tada: Thanks. Quick follow-up: for CI we want a ServiceAccount — what's the recommended pattern for creating tokens that CI can use (without using my personal creds)?

sam: for CI we recommend a limited ServiceAccount in the repo namespace (or a dedicated `ci` namespace) with only the minimal verbs. Example flow:
```
kubectl create serviceaccount ci-sa -n maria-dev
kubectl create role ci-role -n maria-dev --verb=get,list,watch --resource=pods,configmaps
kubectl create rolebinding ci-rolebinding -n maria-dev --role=ci-role --serviceaccount=maria-dev:ci-sa
kubectl create token ci-sa -n maria-dev  # prints a token you can put into secrets manager
```
Store the token in Secrets Manager (AWS Secrets Manager / Vault) and never check it into repo. If you need automatic rotation use the `rctl` token-provisioner integration — ping eng-infra for access.

maria: perfect, will do. Appreciate the quick help everyone!
